title: CyberView: high-priority cyber events
description: High-severity incidents, exploited vulnerabilities and urgent advisories, with what to do, researched and written by CyberView AI (a Claude model). Unverified claims are left out.

items.title: Cybernews reports POS terminals infected via old Windows flaw CVE-2024-49138, data of at least a million bank cards stolen
items.content_text:
Cybernews researchers report that hundreds of POS terminals in many countries, most in Brazil, were infected and that data of at least a million bank cards was stolen. Per the reports, attackers used CVE-2024-49138, a Windows Common Log File System driver flaw that Microsoft fixed in December 2024, to gain higher privileges and then installed a remote access trojan. Detik says exploit code for the flaw is public. The attackers are not named.

What to do: General advice: confirm that point-of-sale Windows systems have Microsoft's December 2024 fix for CVE-2024-49138, as the reports say it has been available since then.

CVEs: CVE-2024-49138

items.title: GreyNoise reports GT13 intrusion campaign against Check Point Security Management Servers affecting at least 22 organisations
items.content_text:
GreyNoise says an actor it tracks as GT13 used 99 IP addresses against Check Point Security Management Servers, with confirmed attack activity between October 17th and November 2nd, 2026, impacting at least 22 distinct organizations globally. GreyNoise says the actor launched over 100 management tasks and obtained command results and data stolen from 24 distinct servers; it lists CVE-2026-16232 among the flaws. It does not attribute GT13 to any known group.

What to do: Check Point advises installing its jumbo hotfix for CVE-2026-16232 (July 2026), limiting Trusted Clients (GUI clients) to trusted IP addresses and restricting Management access to trusted IP addresses.

CVEs: CVE-2026-16232, CVE-2026-61500

items.title: iTerm2 3.7.9 fixes command execution via crafted files displayed in the terminal; researcher publishes proof of concept
items.content_text:
iTerm2's 3.7.9 release notes, built on 20 November, say it fixes a security issue where a crafted file displayed in the terminal, for example with cat, could run arbitrary commands by abusing the Kitty image and drag-and-drop protocols. Researcher Minseong Kim of NSHC Red Alert Labs, credited by iTerm2, lists versions 3.6.1 – 3.7.8 as affected with default settings and has published proof-of-concept exploit code.

What to do: Update iTerm2 to 3.7.9, which iTerm2's release notes say fixes the issue; Cyber Security News also advises not printing raw contents of unfamiliar files into iTerm2 until then.

items.title: Norway's NSM says an unknown actor went after secrets in Azure API Management; Equinor and Skagerak Energi among affected
items.content_text:
Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) says an unknown actor actively went after access tokens, secrets and named values in Azure API Management, and names Equinor and Skagerak Energi among affected organisations. NSM says the vulnerability should now be closed but affects several sectors in and beyond Norway. The Register, citing a nonpublic Microsoft advisory, reports Microsoft identified the issue on 18 November, applied a mitigation the next day, and that only Classic tiers were affected.

What to do: NSM advises organisations using Azure API Management to assume all secrets and named values are compromised and rotate all tokens and secrets, check the gateway's RuntimeVersion against NSM's patch thresholds, contact the vendor if not updated, and contact NSM on signs of compromise.

items.title: Unpatched ASP.NET anti-CSRF library Idunno.AntiCsrf flaw CVE-2026-131914 exploited, Mandiant says
items.content_text:
Mandiant's advisory says CVE-2026-131914 (CVSS 9.3), an insecure deserialization flaw in the legacy ASP.NET module Idunno.AntiCsrf version 0.9.1.0 / 0.9.1 Beta, is being exploited: "Active exploitation in the wild has been observed." According to Mandiant, the project is defunct, with no active maintainer or official patch. The Hacker News reports exploitation needs no prior authentication.

What to do: Mandiant advises organizations to discontinue use of Idunno.AntiCsrf (Idunno.AntiCsrf.dll) and replace it with an actively supported anti-CSRF alternative, and to audit Web.config files and bin/ directories for references to it.

CVEs: CVE-2026-131914

items.title: CISA adds SAP NetWeaver flaw CVE-2025-42884 to its known-exploited catalog
items.content_text:
CISA's alert of 20 November lists SAP NetWeaver CVE-2025-42884 among four vulnerabilities added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation. Heise reports the flaw is a JNDI injection in NetWeaver Enterprise Portal, rated CVSS 6.5, that SAP fixed in its November 2025 Patchday.

What to do: General advice: confirm SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal has the fix SAP released in its November 2025 Patchday.

CVEs: CVE-2025-42884

items.title: KEPCO says personal data of over one and a half million people leaked from its customer and procurement systems
items.content_text:
KEPCO said on 22 November it confirmed on 20 November a leak from Hanjeon ON and the SRM procurement system: 1,520,248 people by simple sum (Newsis, Seoul Economic Daily), overlap unchecked (Dailian). Exposed: ID, bank account and card numbers. Dailian says KEPCO presumes an outside attacker; BleepingComputer says a user called Noiem claimed it on 19 November, unconfirmed. On 24 November KEPCO said it had no further contact with the hacker (Newsis).

What to do: KEPCO urges caution with calls, texts and emails that impersonate KEPCO or come from unclear sources, and runs a dedicated service where customers can check whether their data leaked and report damage.

items.title: Poland's ePUAP e-government platform restricted after cyberattack; full operation restored 19 November, COI says
items.content_text:
Poland’s COI told Sekurak it preventively restricted access to part of the ePUAP system from 10 November, that the attack was detected and stopped, and that full operation returned on 19 November. Deputy PM Krzysztof Gawkowski said the attack came from abroad and that logs showed preparatory activity for a December operation against public administration. COI says the ABW is investigating and it found no sign of spread.

What to do: No action needed; for awareness.

items.title: ZOZO: about 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN customers' data leaked via PLAID KARTE breach
items.content_text:
ZOZO said on 20 November that customer information it managed on PLAID's KARTE leaked. About 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN customers incl. former members (member ID, age, gender, postal code) are affected, about 47,000 of them also with login name, email and phone number; about 13.93 million WEAR by ZOZO customers; about 24,000 brand staff. Passwords are not managed in KARTE; card data is not confirmed leaked.

What to do: ZOZO customers: be wary of phishing emails, texts or calls impersonating ZOZO, and do not open their links or attachments, as ZOZO advises.

items.title: SMBC says up to about 14 million customer records leaked via PLAID KARTE breach
items.content_text:
SMBC said on 20 November that up to about 14 million records of customer information leaked after unauthorized access to KARTE, a service from its contractor PLAID. The data is dates of birth, category values for age band, gender and whether a phone number is registered, and notice flags; SMBC says it is not linked to names and cannot identify individuals. No impact on assets or transactions is confirmed so far.

What to do: SMBC says it will never ask for passwords or card details by email or phone about this; it urges customers not to open links or attachments in suspicious messages claiming to be from the bank.

items.title: Marui Group: about 8.83 million and about 8.5 million customer records leaked via PLAID KARTE breach
items.content_text:
Marui Group said on 20 November that customer data leaked after unauthorized access to PLAID's KARTE, which it says came from PLAID's system, not Marui's. About 8.83 million people (name, gender, date of birth, email, customer management number) and about 8.5 million EPOS CARD users incl. former members (customer management number, gender) are affected; about 60,000 of them may also have name, age, annual income and cash-advance limit exposed. Card numbers are not confirmed leaked.

What to do: Marui and EPOS CARD customers: be careful with suspicious emails and do not open URLs in them or enter personal information, as Marui Group advises.

items.title: Amazon: attackers used the Cairn AI tool to exploit a MONAI Label zero-day and take over a server, BleepingComputer reports
items.content_text:
Amazon found AI agents running the Cairn tool exploiting a path traversal zero-day in MONAI Label, a medical imaging application, within 11 minutes of mapping its API, BleepingComputer reports. They gained root on a server. Amazon attributes it to a Chinese-nexus actor with moderate confidence. ENISA lists CVE-2026-133968; The Hacker News says CISA added it to its KEV catalog.

What to do: ENISA's record lists MONAI Label versions before 0.8.6 as affected; follow the maintainers' advisory GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94, which BleepingComputer links as the security update.

CVEs: CVE-2026-133968

items.title: React2STEAL: GitHub Actions scanners exploit React2Shell and publish stolen secrets
items.content_text:
OpenSourceMalware published research on November 18 on a campaign it named React2STEAL: 45 GitHub repositories across 44 accounts run scanners for React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182) and CVE-2025-29927 and commit results to public repositories. It found at least 1,281 victim hostnames across about 1,100 domains. It lists the actor as unknown. GitGuardian's write-up says patches for both flaws have been available for months.

What to do: Upgrade React and Next.js to fixed versions; until then strip or reject the x-middleware-subrequest header at the proxy or WAF, check logs for it and for /_next/image requests aimed at the metadata address, rotate every secret the server could reach, and enforce IMDSv2.

CVEs: CVE-2025-55182, CVE-2025-29927

items.title: Huntress: attackers exploit ScreenConnect flaw CVE-2026-84869 against MSP technicians' workstations
items.content_text:
Huntress reports attackers exploiting CVE-2026-84869 in ScreenConnect, which lets a guest push files that run on a technician's machine. It saw one full compromise of an MSP technician workstation on November 12 and, since October 20, at least 688,000 guest 'run file' requests for update*.bat hitting 42 MSP servers from 29 IP addresses. Huntress recommends updating technician host clients to 26.6.5 or later; updating the server alone does not fix it.

What to do: Update every technician's ScreenConnect host client to 26.6.5 or later; if you cannot, remove the TransferFiles permission from roles and session groups, as ConnectWise advises, and check Session.db for guest RanFiles or SentFiles events.

CVEs: CVE-2026-84869

items.title: Santos port authority systems still partly down after 6 November outage and cyber intrusion; Federal Police investigating
items.content_text:
Santos Port Authority (APS) systems went down on 6 November. Gazeta do Povo (13 November) reports a Federal Police inquiry opened on 10 November and that hackers emailed APS seeking contact, unanswered. APS's own 17 November notice says a power outage shut its datacentres, then an intrusion erased data; cargo handling was never compromised. ABC do ABC (18 November) says more than 30 systems still run alternatively and APS says no confidential data leaked.

What to do: General advice: port users and shippers should rely only on channels announced by the Autoridade Portuária de Santos, and treat unexpected emails or calls about cargo, access or payments with caution.

items.title: Google: ARMORY CASTLE exploits vCenter zero-day CVE-2026-123890 in espionage campaign
items.content_text:
Google Threat Intelligence Group says ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor it formerly tracked as UNC5221, exploited CVE-2026-123890, an unauthenticated authentication bypass in VMware vCenter Server, from early September 2026. SecurityWeek reports a CVSS of 9.8 and fixes in vCenter 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 and 9.1.1.0200, with no public patch for 7.0. Google names no victims.

What to do: Google advises applying Broadcom's patches immediately; SecurityWeek lists fixed vCenter builds 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 and 9.1.1.0200 and says 7.0 has no public patch. Google also advises restricting inbound access to and egress from vCenter, as described in its post.

CVEs: CVE-2026-123890, CVE-2026-102764

items.title: Cisco Expressway clustering flaw CVE-2026-76466 exploited after public PoC, F6 reports
items.content_text:
Cisco's critical advisory (CVSS 9.8) says an unauthenticated remote attacker can run commands as root on clustered Expressway-C and Expressway-E. SecurityWeek reports F6 investigated an attack on two internet-exposed X15.5.3 devices that spread to two cluster nodes after a GitHub PoC; Security Affairs says the victim was a Russian organization. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 20 November, Help Net Security reports. Fix: X15.5.20.

What to do: If you run clustered Expressway, upgrade to X15.5.20 or later now (X14 and earlier must move to a fixed release; Cisco says no workaround). If you cannot patch at once, F6 advises restricting TCP 4371-4372 at the firewall to trusted cluster node IPs.

CVEs: CVE-2026-76466

items.title: SonicWall: retire Gen 6 firewalls now, no more patches even for critical flaws
items.content_text:
SonicWall's advisory of 18 November says every Gen 6 and Gen 6.5 firewall running SonicOS 6.x, including NSv, has reached end of support and will get no firmware or security patches regardless of severity. SonicWall says it expects internet-facing Gen 6 units to be actively targeted and tells customers to replace them with Gen 8. No new CVE is named.

What to do: Inventory every Gen 6 unit; replace internet-facing ones first; meanwhile disable WAN management and SSL VPN (or restrict sources), enforce MFA, and monitor logs.

items.title: N-able says attackers accessed a Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud server
items.content_text:
N-able says unknown actors accessed one server in its hosted Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud, and it found no evidence customer data was compromised. N-able told SecurityWeek exploitation was confined to a single hosted server and the impacted functionality is restored. Per The Hacker News, a separate SSRF flaw, CVE-2026-134624 (CVSS 4.0 score 9.3), was found during the investigation; N-able has not said whether it was the way in.

What to do: As The Hacker News reports N-able's advisory, SpamExperts Local Cloud operators should confirm they run build 20261121.1943; Hosted Cloud users have nothing to install. N-able told SecurityWeek it revoked customer API tokens and reset local-user passwords.

CVEs: CVE-2026-134624

items.title: WordPress 7.1.5 security release fixes unauthenticated privilege escalation and SQL injection
items.content_text:
WordPress 7.1.5, released November 18, is a security release; Patchstack counts twenty fixes. They include unauthenticated privilege escalation through Template Part block attributes that the project says could lead to remote code execution, two SQL injections, a Multisite Super Admin takeover and stored XSS in comments. The project recommends updating immediately and its post does not mention exploitation.

What to do: WordPress.org recommends updating your sites immediately (Dashboard > Updates > Update Now); sites with automatic background updates will update automatically.

items.title: Bulgaria says hackers had access to government networks for about five years
items.content_text:
Bulgaria's digital minister Ivan Vassilev said that since 2021 more than 130 GB, or 62 million pages, of documents had been downloaded from state networks. Per Reuters, several international hacking groups are believed responsible, with no conclusive foreign-government link. The ministry says the intruders are officially unattributed, first reached infrastructure used to exchange information in 2021, and were found by the new national cybersecurity system. It found no evidence citizens' personal data was compromised.

What to do: No action needed; for awareness. General advice: government and critical-sector defenders should review document-exchange systems for long-dwell access and centralise monitoring.

items.title: DHC: about 19.11 million customer records leaked via PLAID KARTE breach
items.content_text:
DHC announced on November 18 that about 19.11 million online-shop customer records leaked after unauthorized access to PLAID's KARTE marketing service; Business+IT says PLAID told DHC of the intrusion on November 13. Leaked items include names, email addresses and dates of birth; login passwords and card payment data were not included, and DHC says no misuse has been confirmed. DHC plans to report jointly with PLAID to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission.

What to do: General advice: DHC customers should treat unexpected emails or texts using your name and birth date as phishing; change reused passwords.

items.title: Rakuten Securities second report: leaked customer data includes names, addresses and phone numbers
items.content_text:
Rakuten Securities said on 17 November that a third party may have accessed its systems, and test-environment data may have leaked. In its second report of 24 November, relayed by Impress Watch, it said customer codes and login IDs of about 11.98 million accounts leaked, and about 4.41 million records also hold names, birth dates, addresses and phone numbers. The company said no password or PIN leak and no unauthorised trades were confirmed.

What to do: Rakuten Securities advises customers to be careful with suspicious emails, SMS messages, phone calls and mail, and to set up passkey authentication.

items.title: Chile's Huatacondo solar plant still offline almost three months after cyberattack recorded by grid operator
items.content_text:
Chile's Coordinador Eléctrico Nacional recorded the forced disconnection of the 103 MW Huatacondo solar plant and its 98 MW/312 MWh battery system on 27 August with the cause 'cyberattack'; its 14 November report still showed both at 0% availability. The Coordinador says an investigation remains ongoing. Tarapacá's regional energy secretary told La Estrella de Iquique, relayed by Emol, the plant stays disconnected for the owner's reasons. No technical cause or reconnection date is public.

What to do: General advice: operators of solar, storage and thermal plants should confirm that remote access paths and telecontrol are monitored and that their incident-reporting steps are rehearsed.

items.title: Drupal reports core flaw CVE-2026-132165 exploited on live sites; fixed in 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13
items.content_text:
Drupal rates SA-CORE-2026-017, CVE-2026-132165, highly critical: under specific conditions install.php can be used to reinstall a site, leading to takeover or code execution. In an update to the advisory, Drupal says its Security Team received a report this was exploited on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC. Fixed in 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13. A second advisory, CVE-2026-132166, is a gadget chain that is not directly exploitable.

What to do: Drupal advises updating core to 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13; if you cannot upgrade, secure the installer as Drupal describes. Older branches are end of life, per Drupal.

CVEs: CVE-2026-132165, CVE-2026-132166

items.title: CISA adds four exploited flaws to KEV: Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis, REDCap
items.content_text:
CISA added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 18, citing evidence of active exploitation: CVE-2024-10441 in Synology DiskStation Manager, CVE-2026-40217 in BerriAI LiteLLM (unprotected alternate channel), CVE-2026-90436 in Apache Axis (unsafe reflection) and CVE-2026-90817 in Vanderbilt University REDCap (code injection). The alert gives no fixed versions. The Hacker News reports exploitation including ransomware on Synology NAS, cryptomining and LLMjacking.

What to do: CISA directs federal agencies to remediate under BOD 26-04: find Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap in your environment and apply vendor fixes where they exist. The Hacker News reports Axis 1.x is end of life and unpatched, and names migrating or applying the July 12, 2026 commit as options.

CVEs: CVE-2024-10441, CVE-2026-40217, CVE-2026-90436, CVE-2026-90817

items.title: SANS honeypots see scans for chained LiteLLM and Starlette flaws (CVE-2026-42271, CVE-2026-48710)
items.content_text:
SANS ISC honeypots recorded requests to /mcp-rest/test/tools/list attempting to chain CVE-2026-42271 in LiteLLM with CVE-2026-48710 in Starlette for unauthenticated remote code execution. Starlette before 1.0.1 does not validate the Host header. SANS cites a Horizon3.ai write-up and says exploitation has been reported since July. Whether any attempts succeeded is not stated.

What to do: Upgrade Starlette to 1.0.1 or later, update LiteLLM, keep LiteLLM off the public internet, and rotate provider keys on any exposed instance.

CVEs: CVE-2026-42271, CVE-2026-48710

items.title: CERT-FR: NGINX flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution over HTTP/2; public PoC exists
items.content_text:
CERT-FR warns that two flaws in F5 NGINX, CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, allow unauthenticated remote code execution over HTTP/2; a public proof of concept exists for CVE-2026-123007. Fixed in Open Source 1.31.9 and 1.30.7. Palo Alto Networks says PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled are affected and it is not aware of malicious exploitation. Disabling HTTP/2 is an interim workaround for those two flaws.

What to do: CERT-FR recommends applying F5's fixes (bulletins K000163926 and K000163928; Open Source 1.30.7 or 1.31.9) and, until patched, disabling HTTP/2, which covers only the HTTP/2 flaws. Palo Alto Networks says PAN-OS and Panorama customers can disable the HTTP/2 option.

CVEs: CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123634, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-113425

items.title: Microsoft Agent Framework PyPI package compromised with credential stealer
items.content_text:
Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of the agent-framework package on PyPI were published on November 17 with a credential stealer that runs when Python starts, targeting cloud, GitHub and AI credentials and tokens. PyPI quarantined both; 1.26.0 is the last safe version. Italy's CSIRT (ACN) says the malware installed no OS-level persistence and downloaded no further payloads. Xakep.ru reports Microsoft said it made some repositories private during the investigation; the entry route is unknown.

What to do: Wiz and CSIRT Italia advise pinning agent-framework to 1.26.0, checking lockfiles, CI logs and environments for 1.26.1 or 1.26.2, and rotating credentials and tokens exposed to any host that installed them.

items.title: Apache warns Roller RCE flaw (CVE-2026-129448) is exploited in attacks
items.content_text:
Apache says an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in Roller, CVE-2026-129448, is being exploited. It is a deserialization bug in the XML-RPC interface affecting versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4, and is the same bug as CVE-2026-82384, which named only 6.1.5. Version 6.1.6 or later fixes it. Italy's CSIRT (ACN) reported active exploitation on 23 November.

What to do: Apache advises upgrading Roller to 6.1.6 or later. If you cannot, Apache says to set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping, then restart Roller; switching off XML-RPC in the admin UI is not enough.

CVEs: CVE-2026-129448

items.title: NCSC Netherlands: public exploit code for critical Ivanti Endpoint Manager flaw (CVE-2026-121653)
items.content_text:
The Dutch National Cyber Security Centre warns that proof-of-concept code is now public for CVE-2026-121653, an SQL injection flaw in the Core of Ivanti Endpoint Manager before 2024 SU8. A remote attacker without credentials can use it to run code. A second flaw, CVE-2026-18128, lets an attacker positioned on the network read and alter agent traffic sent in clear text. Ivanti has released updates.

What to do: Install the updates Ivanti has released for Endpoint Manager, as the NCSC-NL advisory advises; see Ivanti's November 2026 security advisory for affected versions and fixes.

CVEs: CVE-2026-121653, CVE-2026-18128

items.title: Japan's RIKEN takes Fugaku supercomputer offline after intrusion
items.content_text:
RIKEN's first notice says an outside party reached Fugaku's internal operational network from November 10 to 13 through a public web page showing Fugaku's operational status; the exact method is under investigation. Its second notice (20 Nov) lists 4,222 Fugaku users as affected and says 430 credentials (233 SSH private keys without a passphrase, 197 with one) were exfiltrated; some were used for external connections. Fugaku stays offline; no attacker is named.

What to do: Fugaku users: revoke and replace SSH keys used with Fugaku, as RIKEN asks, and watch for phishing emails. Others: no action needed; for awareness.

items.title: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Microsoft November rollup AV26-1142 updated for exploited flaw CVE-2026-124194
items.content_text:
Cyber Centre advisory AV26-1142 relays Microsoft's November 2026 security updates to Canadian organisations. The affected list spans Windows 10 and 11, Windows Server 2012 to 2025, Microsoft 365 Apps and Office, Exchange Server Subscription Edition, SharePoint Server, SQL Server, .NET, Visual Studio and many Azure services. Update 1, dated November 12, adds that Microsoft reports CVE-2026-124194 as exploited and that CISA catalogued it on November 10.

What to do: Install Microsoft's November 2026 security updates across Windows, Office, Exchange, SharePoint, SQL Server and developer tools, taking the fix for CVE-2026-124194 first. Use the MSRC release notes linked from the advisory to scope the work.

CVEs: CVE-2026-124194

items.title: NCSC New Zealand alerts on OpenSSH 'SSHole' authentication bypass CVE-2026-123158
items.content_text:
New Zealand's NCSC issued an alert on November 11 about CVE-2026-123158, nicknamed SSHole, an authentication bypass in OpenSSH on Linux that may give an attacker root access. A system is exposed only if it runs a version before 10.6p2, uses musl libc, does not use PAM and accepts password logins. The alert does not say whether the flaw is being exploited.

What to do: Identify Linux systems running OpenSSH before 10.6p2 on musl libc without PAM that accept password logins, and update to 10.6p2. Until then, disable password authentication or turn SSH off on those systems.

CVEs: CVE-2026-123158

items.title: CERT-EU rates Citrix NetScaler flaws critical: unauthenticated memory overflows scored up to 9.5
items.content_text:
CERT-EU Security Advisory 2026-020 covers 28 memory flaws in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway. CVE-2026-120868, scored 9.3, sits in core packet processing and affects every deployment, default configuration included, without authentication. CVE-2026-107412, scored 9.5, affects appliances set up as a Gateway or AAA virtual server. Citrix reports no exploitation and no public proof of concept is confirmed.

What to do: Upgrade customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway to 14.1-73.57 or 13.1-64.39, FIPS builds to 14.1-73.58 FIPS or 13.1-37.293. Do internet-facing Gateway and AAA appliances first.

CVEs: CVE-2026-120868, CVE-2026-107412

items.title: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Check Point advisory AV26-1154 updated to note an exploited flaw
items.content_text:
Cyber Centre advisory AV26-1154, issued November 12 and updated the next day, covers two flaws across multiple versions of Check Point Force firewalls, management and log servers, Multi-Domain products and Maestro Orchestrator. It relays Check Point's statement that CVE-2026-123039, a local escalation to root, is being exploited in the wild. Update 1 records that CISA added that flaw to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalog on November 13.

What to do: Apply Check Point's fixes for CVE-2026-123039 and CVE-2026-107484 on firewalls, management and log servers, Multi-Domain servers and Maestro Orchestrator. Read the Check Point advisories and the CISA catalog entry linked from the advisory.

CVEs: CVE-2026-123039, CVE-2026-107484

items.title: CSA Singapore warns of active exploitation of Apache HTTP Server mod_http2 flaw CVE-2026-119618
items.content_text:
Singapore's Cyber Security Agency issued alert AL-2026-164 on November 17 about CVE-2026-119618, rated 8.1, in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2, affecting 2.4.55 up to but not including 2.4.71. The agency says exploitation is reportedly under way and proof-of-concept code is public. Apache lists it as critical and fixed in 2.4.71. Praetorian says a worker thread modifying a shared headers table is the cause, and it has no working remote code execution exploit yet.

What to do: As CSA urges, update affected Apache HTTP Server installations (2.4.55 to before 2.4.71 with mod_http2 enabled) to the latest version immediately; the Apache advisory lists 2.4.71 as the fixed release.

CVEs: CVE-2026-119618

items.title: CISA adds exploited Perforce Puppet Enterprise flaw (CVE-2026-115731) to KEV
items.content_text:
CISA added CVE-2026-115731, a deserialization flaw in Perforce Puppet Enterprise, to its KEV catalog on November 17, citing active exploitation; Help Net Security says federal agencies must fix it by December 1. It reports a client holding a Puppet CA-signed certificate can send a crafted report and run code as the Puppet Server user. Fixed in 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1 and 2023.8.13.

What to do: Perforce advises upgrading Puppet Enterprise to 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1 or 2023.8.13 (Puppet Core 9.1.3 or 8.22.2), restarting the server as soon as possible, and reviewing autosign configuration as a temporary mitigation, per Help Net Security.

CVEs: CVE-2026-115731

items.title: Dragos counts 1,266 ransomware incidents at industrial organisations in Q3 2026
items.content_text:
Dragos recorded 1,266 ransomware incidents affecting industrial organisations in the third quarter of 2026, up 11% from 1,140 the quarter before. Manufacturing took 69% of them and the United States 37%. According to Dragos, Qilin led with 195 incidents, ahead of The Gentlemen (167 claimed victims) and Cl0p (35). Dragos names exploited edge devices and enterprise applications, and stolen VPN credentials, among the ways in. Dragos saw no operator directly manipulate an industrial control system.

What to do: Dragos recommends rotating administrator and VPN credentials, especially on FortiGate appliances, enforcing MFA on all remote access, auditing for administrator accounts not created internally, and patching edge devices rapidly.

CVEs: CVE-2026-0257, CVE-2026-15409, CVE-2026-15410, CVE-2026-63077, CVE-2026-59310, CVE-2026-12569

items.title: Rapid7 and CISA: critical Java flaw CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell) in Java 17 and later; Oracle patches released
items.content_text:
Rapid7 and CISA warn of CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell), a memory corruption bug in the x86-64 HotSpot JVM Base64 decoder that could allow remote code execution; Oracle released fixes on November 17. SecurityWeek (Nov 19) reports GreyNoise saw over 150 matching requests from five IP addresses, with no successful intrusions seen on its sensors; Cisco, Siemens, Elastic and Red Hat issued advisories.

What to do: Inventory every Java runtime, including bundled ones, and install the fixed releases (for example 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, 27.0.1.1), internet-facing systems first. See Rapid7's advisory for compensating controls where patching is not possible.

CVEs: CVE-2026-114938

items.title: MS-ISAC: SonicWall SonicOS flaws allow authentication bypass; one SSLVPN bug is already on CISA's KEV list
items.content_text:
MS-ISAC advisory 2026-126 covers seven flaws in SonicWall SonicOS on Gen7 firewalls up to 7.3.3-7015 and Gen8 up to 8.2.2-8015. Two management-interface bugs let remote unauthenticated attackers perform unauthorised operations under certain conditions. CVE-2026-19868 lets a user with other valid credentials skip SAML, and possibly MFA, on SSLVPN; SonicWall investigated a report of exploitation and CISA listed it as exploited on November 6.

What to do: Apply SonicWall's SonicOS updates for Gen7 and Gen8 firewalls after testing, starting with devices using SAML for SSLVPN, and keep firewall management interfaces off the internet.

CVEs: CVE-2026-107154, CVE-2026-107155, CVE-2026-19703, CVE-2026-19868, CVE-2026-82308, CVE-2026-77708, CVE-2026-77709

items.title: FBI: FLASH details North Korean FaceStealer fake-meeting scheme behind $400M in crypto theft
items.content_text:
FBI FLASH AC-111226-MS (TLP:CLEAR) attributes the FaceStealer scheme to North Korean state-sponsored hackers (Sapphire Sleet, UNC1069, BlueNoroff). They hijack a victim's messaging account, invite contacts to a counterfeit Zoom or Teams call, replay recorded webcam video and push a fake audio fix that installs malware. The FBI says over $400 million was stolen in about 18 months.

What to do: Join calls through the official Zoom or Teams app with an invite code, keep the webcam off until the host is verified another way, never run scripts or paste code to fix audio, and enable MFA and login alerts on messaging accounts.

items.title: CISA: six industrial control advisories cover Siemens building, edge and RUGGEDCOM products
items.content_text:
CISA released six industrial control system advisories on November 12: five for Siemens products (building automation and energy, Desigo and Gridscale, Industrial Edge Management and two for RUGGEDCOM APE1808) and an update for Hitachi Energy RTU500. One RUGGEDCOM advisory covers a Brotli decoder flaw in the bundled PAN-OS, rated 9.8, that a remote unauthenticated attacker could use to crash the device or possibly run code.

What to do: Operators of the listed Siemens and Hitachi Energy products: read the matching advisory. For RUGGEDCOM APE1808, upgrade PAN-OS to a corrected version, restrict network access to the device and keep it off the internet.

CVEs: CVE-2026-111497

items.title: Caixa Vida e Previdência breach exposes data of 7.6 million clients in Brazil
items.content_text:
The insurer and pension company, part of Caixa Seguridade, said on November 12 it detected unauthorized access on November 6 and that registration data was copied. Per Estadão Conteúdo, the base covers all 7.6 million active clients plus ex-clients; names and CPFs for all records, other details for part. It says no financial or authentication data appears affected, and it notified ANPD on November 11.

What to do: General advice: if you are a Caixa Vida e Previdência client, be wary of calls, emails or messages that cite your CPF or policy, do not share codes or passwords, and use the company's official channel for questions.

items.title: eMudhra revokes eight more CAs as Microsoft pulls trust in all its roots
items.content_text:
iTnews reports the Indian certificate authority eMudhra revoked eight more intermediate CAs; its incident report says a single line in a homebrew Python script truncated ECDSA private values to their leading byte. iTnews says Microsoft will remove all 10 remaining eMudhra roots from 16 November, and eMudhra said Apple would end trust on 30 November. iTnews also says eMudhra is leaving public TLS and has withdrawn its RSA assurance.

What to do: General advice: inventory certificates chaining to eMudhra roots and replace them with certificates from another CA, and apply current Windows and macOS updates.

items.title: Attackers exploit Apache Axis flaw CVE-2026-90436 in Confluence Data Center
items.content_text:
Rapid7 says its MDR team detected exploitation of CVE-2026-90436 against a customer's Confluence Data Center on November 13. The flaw is unauthenticated remote code execution in end-of-life Apache Axis 1.x, reachable when Confluence's Remote API is enabled. The intruder harvested database credentials, queried a cloud data warehouse and later signed in to Microsoft 365 as a service account. Confluence 9.2.28 fixes it; Cloud is unaffected.

What to do: Rapid7 advises upgrading Confluence Data Center to 9.2.28 or a current 10.x release, internet-facing systems first; if you cannot, clear the Remote API (XML-RPC & SOAP) setting, and investigate exposed systems with the indicators Rapid7 published.

CVEs: CVE-2026-90436

items.title: Openwave Webtop Media Transcoder: file-type restriction bypass added to CISA exploited list
items.content_text:
The Webtop Media Transcoder does not enforce the file-type limits an administrator sets, so a signed-in user who goes around the Webmail interface can have it process and convert document types that were meant to be blocked. CISA lists the flaw as exploited and set a federal due date of 2026-11-24.

What to do: Apply the vendor's mitigations, check each affected system's internet exposure and follow CISA's BOD 26-04 triage guidance; stop using the transcoder if no mitigation is available. Federal due date is November 24.

CVEs: CVE-2026-111793

items.title: SignDrop: researcher releases Windows zero-day giving SYSTEM privileges
items.content_text:
A researcher using the name MSNightmare published SignDrop on November 10, an unpatched Windows flaw that lifts a standard user to SYSTEM by abusing CLFS log authentication and Microsoft Defender's signature-update interface. Cyderes reproduced it in a controlled environment and got a SYSTEM shell. There is no CVE or patch; as of November 11 Microsoft had not commented, and no use in real attacks had been confirmed.

What to do: No patch exists. Limit who can run untrusted software with application control, do not disable CLFS authentication, deploy Cyderes's detections for the Defender update interface and unexpected hid.dll files, and apply Microsoft's fix when released.

items.title: Unpatched Check Point gateways wiped in PHP2Shell attacks
items.content_text:
Check Point says attackers chained the PHP2Shell flaws in the Mobile Access Portal with a Gaia privilege escalation to gain root on unpatched gateways from October 30, a week after a fix on October 23. A first wave hit Israeli organisations, destructive in some cases; a second wave from November 2 reached several countries without destruction. Check Point says only a couple of dozen unpatched systems were compromised.

What to do: Check Point advises installing the November Jumbo Hotfix on all Management Servers and Security Gateways, starting with internet-facing Mobile Access deployments. Hunt for the published indicators and ask Check Point Support for an exposure assessment.

CVEs: CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, CVE-2026-123039

items.title: German military grounds Quantum Systems drones after cyberattack on the maker
items.content_text:
Quantum Systems confirmed an active cyberattack by "hostile actors", noticed in October, that it says its teams contained. Der Spiegel and the Financial Times, as relayed by Security Affairs and Euronews, report attackers may have used a malicious update and that the German military stopped using its drones; on 13 November the company told Reuters they were flying again. Per dpa, Bamberg's Generalstaatsanwaltschaft is investigating against unknown persons. No attacker is named.

What to do: Quantum Systems says there is no risk in operating its unmanned systems for end users and operators, per Reuters; no other advice is given.

items.title: Cursor says exposed Fireworks AI key led to malicious Claude Code extension copies
items.content_text:
Cursor's November 13 update says an access key it had issued to Fireworks AI was exposed by that supplier and used to copy coding agent traces from a read-only bucket. Credentials found in the traces let the attacker reach select SaaS tools used by Cursor. On October 29 the attacker placed malicious Claude Code extension builds 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 in Cursor's marketplace cache for about 11 hours; at most 5,000 users potentially received them.

What to do: Cursor asks users who installed or updated to Claude Code extension 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 on October 29 to follow its security notice (uninstalling alone may not be enough); it emailed team admins the specific keys to rotate.

items.title: Huntress: rogue ScreenConnect clients pushed to hundreds of hosts in SCKit attacks; ConnectWise disables extensions
items.content_text:
Huntress reports two waves of attacks, on November 11 and November 13, using ScreenConnect's Run Command feature to install rogue clients on at least 288 and then 205 hosts, apparently via a flawed third-party RMM+ extension. SCKit tries to steal a technician's session cookie; Huntress has not seen that succeed. Rapid7 lists CVE-2026-127063 for RMM+'s default static API secret, not affecting ScreenConnect itself; CVE-2026-84869 is named only as background.

What to do: Huntress advises: confirm technician clients run ScreenConnect 26.6.5 or later, disable RMM+ extension 1.0.31 and 1.0.32, review Run Command history, and check endpoints for a second ScreenConnect client. Do not connect to suspect hosts through ScreenConnect.

CVEs: CVE-2026-84869, CVE-2026-127063

items.title: Amazon uncovers AI agent campaign hunting exposed apps for AI provider keys
items.content_text:
Amazon observed two campaigns between October 3 and November 5 that it assesses, with moderate confidence, were run with ARTEX AI agents by Chinese-nexus groups. One hunted internet-exposed AI gateways and app builders for upstream provider keys; the other tried to beat identity checks at two crypto exchanges with real-time deepfake video and forged ID photos. One vendor's server rejected every deepfake attempt the agents recorded.

What to do: Remove default or hardcoded credentials (including the LiteLLM default master key), require login on AI gateways and builders, patch Langflow and RAGFlow, rotate keys ever exposed in code, and watch for unexpected AI spend or usage.

CVEs: CVE-2025-3248, CVE-2026-28797

items.title: Breach at La Poste subsidiary Maileva exposes 22 million people in France
items.content_text:
A cyberattack on Maileva, La Poste's mail-services subsidiary, exposed first names, last names and postal addresses of 22 million people (next.ink: potentially exposed), mostly recipients of mail sent for client organisations. La Poste says the regulator CNIL was notified and a complaint filed; next.ink reports the Paris prosecutor opened an investigation. Maileva says bank details were not compromised. The attack dates from mid-September.

What to do: Organisations using Maileva: ask which of your recipients are affected and whether you must notify them or the regulator. People in France: be wary of letters, calls or messages that use your name and address to seem genuine.

items.title: N-able patches 17 more N-central flaws; exploitation reported, The Hacker News says crypto miners deployed
items.content_text:
N-able says it has been responding since November 9 to N-central zero-days published without coordinated disclosure. Hotfix 2 fixed seven internet-facing flaws; Hotfix 3 fixes 17 more, CVE-2026-129271 to CVE-2026-129287, and permanently removes the Legacy API. The Hacker News reports crypto miners deployed on vulnerable servers, and Rapid7 says N-able reported exploitation on November 13.

What to do: N-able advises on-premises customers to upgrade servers to 2026.4.1.40 (Hotfix 4) as soon as possible, and all Agents and Probes to the same version; hosted servers need no action. Hotfix 3 permanently removes the Legacy API.

CVEs: CVE-2026-90436, CVE-2026-129271, CVE-2026-129272, CVE-2026-129273, CVE-2026-129274, CVE-2026-129275, CVE-2026-129276, CVE-2026-129277, CVE-2026-129278, CVE-2026-129279, CVE-2026-129280, CVE-2026-129281, CVE-2026-129282, CVE-2026-129283, CVE-2026-129284, CVE-2026-129285, CVE-2026-129286, CVE-2026-129287

items.title: Six unpatched Danfoss refrigeration controller flaws allow remote takeover
items.content_text:
Midnight Blue found six pre-authentication remote code execution flaws in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers, affecting firmware up to and including 5.3.2. CVE numbers are pending and details are withheld during coordinated disclosure. The researchers say patching alone will not make these devices safe and that hundreds remain reachable from the internet. Attack waves on such controllers began in France on October 11.

What to do: List every AK-SM800A reachable from the internet, including through integrators' 4G modems, and restrict management access to a VPN, private APN or strict IP whitelist. Put controllers on a separate OT network and change default passwords. Do not rely on patching alone.

items.title: Cyberattack closes emergency room at Greiz-Ronneburg hospital in Germany
items.content_text:
The Greiz district says a cyberattack on its hospital, discovered on November 15, made the emergency room unavailable; state criminal police and prosecutors were called in. Kommunal.de reports the district called it an extortion attempt; on November 17 the district said it could not comment on any demands during the investigation. The district says the emergency room took patients again from November 17 and, on November 18, that operating theatres were fully functional again.

What to do: As the district's notice of 17 November asks, patients with questions about appointments should phone the hospital first. General advice: other hospitals should confirm they can run emergency care without IT.

items.title: Microsoft 365 outage knocks out Outlook, Teams and Copilot in 74 countries
items.content_text:
Outlook, Teams and Copilot were disrupted from 12 November in 74 countries, per Al Jazeera; CyberCube puts the broader incident at about 38 hours. Microsoft's report says its testing did not adequately represent the hardware and traffic mix encountered (KIRO 7). CyberCube's preliminary analysis says insured losses will most likely total less than $100 mn, with a conservative upper bound of $350 mn.

What to do: Microsoft says this was not an attack, so no security action is needed. General advice: confirm that delayed email has arrived, check your agreement for service credits and review how staff communicate when email is down.

items.title: Google warns fully automated AI attacks are arriving
items.content_text:
Google’s November 16 threat report says that, for the first time, it found actors using LLM frameworks to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation with no human in the loop. Code comments are in Russian and server telemetry suggests interest in French media, entertainment and education sites, but Google names no group or state. Other actors are testing agentic tools, and Google expects more autonomy over time.

What to do: Google's report points to Mandiant's hardening guide and architectural defense framework against LLM-enabled offensive tooling. General advice: shorten patch windows for internet-facing systems and check that monitoring can respond to fast automated activity.

CVEs: CVE-2026-81578, CVE-2026-82078, CVE-2026-40217

items.title: NSA's classified internal network NSA Net goes down
items.content_text:
CNN reported, citing six people, that NSA Net went down on 17 November; other sources say service was intermittent. The NSA cites degradation during scheduled routine maintenance; DNI Jay Clayton linked it to PHP patching. CNN's sources said there was no evidence of a cyberattack. On 20 November an NSA spokesperson told Nextgov: "NSA can confirm that we are now operating under normal conditions."

What to do: No action needed; for awareness.
